feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital communications/strategy and credible progression at NACo. It reads well and shows breadth, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional brand: the header summary is focused, relevant, and aligned with the target role.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions at one organization signal trust, growth, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good evidence of scope: website migration, analytics stack expansion, studio buildout, and AI-enabled search all add substance and modern relevance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include metrics such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, adoption rates, campaign results, or cost savings.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; keep comma usage consistent in lists (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one clearer differentiator tied to recent senior-level work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with current senior value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Tighten the channel list to avoid sounding like a skills inventory; emphasize outcomes and leadership scope instead.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that support complex communications operations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies.
- Avoid adding detailed platform/tool references here; those are already covered elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if it emphasizes higher-level strengths and uses parallel, polished phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize wording for consistency: “Multi-channel communications,” “Cross-functional stakeholder coordination,” “Web platform and CMS administration.”
- Replace vague items with sharper, more senior language: “Workflow & systems architecture” → “Content operations and workflow architecture.”
- Reorder for impact and recency: lead with strategy, platform modernization, content operations, analytics, then communications/multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy and transformation • Content operations and workflow architecture • Web platform and CMS administration • Multi-channel communications • Data analytics and performance reporting • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy and advocacy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy & transformation” and “Multi-channel communication” repeat the header and Topline Skills almost verbatim.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” are also covered in detail under Topline Skills/Technical sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the “Recent Projects” section. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and leadership of systems modernization.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets and lead with impact: combine digital systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on improving coordination, publishing efficiency, or reporting.
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet more outcome-driven: mention number of sites, campaigns, toolkits, users, or performance gains if available.
- Rephrase AI search bullet to emphasize ownership and value: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Campaign storytelling experiences,” “AI-enabled search,” and the microsite/toolkit work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language also echoes the NACo Director role; distinguish this role by emphasizing consulting, embedded partnership, and current modernization work.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with solid scale metrics; it should read more crisply as an executive leadership entry and emphasize outcomes over channel inventory. Tighten overlap with earlier NACo roles by focusing on transformation, infrastructure, and team/operating model leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Combine scope + flagship achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Rephrase channels bullet to stress management/results, not just reach; add metrics if possible (email growth, engagement, open rates, follower growth, video output, cost savings).
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets into outcomes: “Built reporting stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership visibility and decision-making”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video program/studio language overlaps with earlier NACo roles and Recent Projects; keep this entry at the strategic/buildout level.
- Editorial coordination and publishing workflow improvements overlap with Associate Director; frame here as enterprise governance.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and specific to systems/editorial coordination rather than broad channel leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points: newsletter ownership, launch/expansion of weekly advocacy video, cross-team editorial planning, and workflow/process improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter audience size, video cadence/views, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, publishing volume, or turnaround improvements.
- Use stronger verbs: “managed,” “produced,” “standardized,” “coordinated,” “streamlined” instead of “helped” and “strengthened.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- Weekly video/livestream language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this role as scaling and formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” are already echoed in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is close to “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills area, make it more strategic and recent by emphasizing platforms plus execution strengths tied to current work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, higher-value phrases rather than standalone tools:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages
- CMS modernization and large-site migration
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations, workflow automation & Airtable-based systems
- AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Put the most marketable/recent items first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, swap one generic item for scope: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the Technical + IT section; keep Topline Skills broader and save full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list rather than a differentiated skill cluster. Since recent roles already show studio buildout and event/video leadership, this item should emphasize scope and delivery strength, not just components.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability + outcomes: “Broadcast-quality video production, livestreaming, and hybrid event delivery”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use this space to sharpen platform credibility and emphasize the most recent, highest-impact CMS work.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent evidence: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider adding context: “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented rather than just a list: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsite and modular content builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep platform names only here; move any implementation detail to the adjacent “Coding & Technical Implementation” section.
- If GitHub Pages is minor compared with enterprise CMS work, consider dropping it to keep the list tighter and more senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Topline Skills” section almost exactly; differentiate by adding brief platform context or trimming one version.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Reorder by relevance/recency: JavaScript • HTML/CSS • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • GitHub Actions • Cloudflare Workers • jQuery
- Simplify outdated formatting: use “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”; move jQuery to the end or remove if no longer central
- If space allows, add scope/context rather than only tools, e.g. “JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, GTM, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” “Workflow automation”); consider trimming one version
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you specifically use it for deployment/technical implementation

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is useful but currently reads as a generic tool list. It should better emphasize systems you actively build or use strategically, while avoiding overlap with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already named in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by strength/relevance: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp”
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a pure list, e.g.: “Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate, Zapier (process automation) • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp (project tracking) • Slack, Microsoft Teams (team coordination)”
- If these tools were central in recent roles, consider replacing 1–2 lower-value names with evidence in experience bullets instead of expanding this list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; keep this section tool-focused, not concept-focused.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; unless used for structured workflow operations, they add less value than automation/platform tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is clear but too bare compared with the rest of the CV. Since email is a major theme in recent roles, this line should signal level of use or scope, not just list tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, audience engagement)”
- If accurate, strengthen further with level: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • enterprise newsletter and campaign platform administration”
- Keep naming consistent with other technical items; avoid the slash-heavy phrasing if possible: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys”
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and credibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated email/newsletter references in NACo roles; don’t restate audience size or newsletter volume here.
- Avoid adding generic terms like “email marketing” if the work experience already demonstrates that clearly.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with 1–2 concrete outputs or scale indicators.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving production workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Add specific contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestream event coverage and weekly video updates for member communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “coordinated day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/events, video cadence, audience reach, or workflow improvements (turnaround time, output volume).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; here, frame it as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific support function such as “produced digital and multimedia content for policy and member-facing communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes launched, internal stakeholders supported, audience/download growth, or types of projects delivered.
- Keep the scope modest and foundational so it reads as the starting point of your NACo progression, not a duplicate of later digital leadership roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with the 2015–2018 and 2018–2024 NACo entries.
- Avoid overstating team leadership or enterprise digital ownership here; those are better established in later roles.
